relations: Suspended prisms on twisted wires drift slowly left while vertical heights stay roughly constant.
Fixed bokeh background makes the swaying cluster appear to slide across it.
Wires tilt progressively, shifting each prism's facet toward the camera.
Orientation changes make rainbow highlights crawl and internal inverted images brighten and slide.
caption: The video showcases several faceted teardrop-shaped crystal prisms suspended from thin twisted wires fitted with small clear beads, hanging against a dark background of round bokeh lights in green, yellow, orange, magenta and cyan. Each prism acts as a lens, its lower half holding an inverted, refracted image of a lit scene with figures and glowing spots. The cluster sways gently, drifting slowly toward the left while the blurred background stays fixed, so the crystals slide against it. The wires tilt progressively, and the shifting viewing angle changes the facet each prism presents to the camera. As the orientation shifts, rainbow highlights crawl across the cut surfaces and the inverted images inside brighten and slide. Vertical positions stay roughly constant, the main change being this gradual drift and small rotational sway that continues throughout.
